## Overview
### Technical Overview
The Google: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview) is a standard-tier model provided by Google, released on January 1, 2024. This model is not open-source and is designed with a specific architecture that supports various capabilities such as text, function calling, JSON mode, streaming, and structured outputs. Its primary strengths lie in its ability to handle a wide range of tasks, including chat, text generation, coding, analysis, RAG pipelines, and summarization.

### Architecture and Pricing
The model's architecture is built to process input and output tokens efficiently, with a context window of 65,536 tokens and a maximum output of 65,536 tokens. The pricing for this model is based on the number of tokens processed, with input tokens costing $0.5 per 1M tokens and output tokens costing $3.0 per 1M tokens. There are no additional costs for cached input or batch input. The knowledge cutoff for this model is December 2023, ensuring that its training data is up to date until that point. Benchmarks for this model include an MMLU score of 80.0 and an LMSYS Arena ELO score of 1200.

### Use Cases and Cost Examples
The Google: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview) is best suited for applications that require advanced text processing, such as chatbots, text generation, coding assistance, and data analysis. The cost of using this model can be estimated based on the number of calls and tokens processed. For example, 1,000 calls with an average of 500 tokens would cost approximately $0.0018, while 100,000 calls would cost around $0.18. With no direct competitors listed, this model offers a unique set of capabilities and pricing that can be beneficial for developers looking to integrate advanced text processing into their applications.
